sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents
- mcp: Use mcp to connect to Streamable HTTP servers, discover tool schemas, and call their tools.

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.
toolsAdded.name: read

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.
toolsAdded.name: bash

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.
toolsAdded.name: edit

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.
toolsAdded.name: write

content.description: Content to write to the file

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.
toolsAdded.name: grep

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).
toolsAdded.name: find

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

toolsAdded.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).
toolsAdded.name: ls

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

## How a forced transaction works

A forced transaction takes the same path as any other Delayed Inbox message. Only the last step differs.

1. **You send a message to the Delayed Inbox on the parent chain.** Each [message type](#what-you-can-force-include) has its own Inbox function. The parent chain records the message and the block it arrived in.
2. **The sequencer picks it up, or the window runs out.** If the sequencer adds the message, the next <Term id="batch">batch</Term> the batch poster posts to the Sequencer Inbox marks it as read. If the sequencer ignores the message until the force-inclusion window ends, anyone can call `forceInclusion`. It posts an empty batch to the Sequencer Inbox that marks the message as read.
3. **Every child-chain node executes it.** Nodes see the message marked as read in the Sequencer Inbox, take its contents from the Delayed Inbox, and execute it in order.

When the sequencer is running, you do not need force inclusion. Most transactions go straight to the sequencer through an RPC endpoint. A message you send to the Delayed Inbox also reaches the chain: the sequencer adds it to a child-chain block, and the batch poster later posts that block to the parent chain.

block that holds your message is marked safe. Three [settings](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/blob/ccc5c828d9ea22f161efc784bac4d4a6559b7e59/arbnode/delayed_sequencer.go#L66-L72) change that wait:

- `node.delayed-sequencer.require-full-finality=true` makes it wait for a finalized block instead of a safe one.
- `node.delayed-sequencer.use-merge-finality=false` makes it wait a fixed number of blocks instead.
- `node.delayed-sequencer.finalize-distance` sets that number of blocks, 20 by default. The sequencer also uses this setting if the parent chain does not report safe and finalized blocks.

## What you can force-include

`forceInclusion` works on every Delayed Inbox message, whatever its type. The message type decides which Inbox function you call and what the child chain does with the message.

| Message                                                                                    | Inbox function                                                                     | What the child chain does with it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A signed child-chain transaction                                                           | `sendL2Message` or `sendL2MessageFromOrigin`                                       | Executes it from your own address, with no aliasing. <Term id="arbos">ArbOS</Term> drops blob (EIP-4844) transactions. Use this to call any contract or to [withdraw ETH](#withdraw-eth-while-the-sequencer-is-down). The [SDK steps](#force-include-a-signed-transaction-with-the-arbitrum-sdk) use this message type.                                                 |
| An ETH deposit

| `depositEth`                                                                       | Credits the ETH to the sender's address on the child chain. If a contract sent the deposit, the ETH goes to the contract's aliased address. The [`force-inclusion` example](#runnable-examples) force-includes a deposit.                                                                                                                                               |
| A <Term id="retryable-ticket">retryable ticket</Term>                                      | `createRetryableTicket`                                                            | Creates the ticket. ArbOS schedules an automatic redemption only if the gas limit is at least 21,000, the fee cap covers the child chain's base fee when the message executes, and the sender's balance covers both. Otherwise, the ticket waits for a manual redemption. See [Retryable tickets](/how-arbitrum-works/deep-dives/l1-to-l2-messaging#retryable-tickets). |
| An [unsigned message](/how-arbitrum-works/deep-dives/l1-to-l2-messaging#unsigned-messages) | `sendUnsignedTransaction`, `sendContractTransaction`, or their `L1Funded` variants | Executes it from the sender's [aliased address](/how-arbitrum-works/deep-dives/l1-to-l2-messaging#address-aliasing).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

For each function's parameters, see [Sending transactions via the Delayed Inbox](/arbitrum-essentials/bridging/deposit/eth-and-messages#sending-transactions-via-the-delayed-inbox).

## The force-inclusion timeline

How your message reaches the chain depends on how long the sequencer stays offline or keeps ignoring it.

| How long the sequencer is offline or ignores your message | What happens to your message                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Not at all                                                | The sequencer adds it once the parent-chain block is safe, by default. See [When the sequencer is running](#when-the-sequencer-is-running). |
| Less than the force-inclusion window                      | It waits in the Delayed Inbox. When the sequencer returns, it adds the message in order. Nobody can force-include it yet.                   |
| Longer than the force-inclusion window                    | Anyone can call `forceInclusion`. The message enters the Sequencer Inbox, and every child-chain node processes it.                          |

### Before the window ends

Your message is safe in the Delayed Inbox, but only the seque

ncer can move it. The Sequencer Inbox reverts any `forceInclusion` call for this message with `ForceIncludeBlockTooSoon`. If the sequencer or someone else already included the message, the call reverts earlier, with `DelayedBackwards`.

The sequencer cannot skip or reorder Delayed Inbox messages. It must process them in the order they arrived.

### After the window ends

The [`forceInclusion`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro-contracts/blob/4341b132cfbdcc980ead03765ca5224ff6cb5d97/src/bridge/SequencerInbox.sol#L273-L330) function succeeds once the current parent-chain block number exceeds your message's block number plus the force-inclusion window.

One call includes your message and every earlier message still waiting in the Delayed Inbox. If someone else force-includes a later message, your message is included too.

<Callout type="info" title="The contract counts blocks, not seconds">

`forceInclusion` checks only parent-chain block numbers. `delayBlocks` is <Var name="arbOneForceIncludePeriodBlocks" /> Ethereum blocks on Arbitrum One and <Var name="novaForceIncludePeriodBlocks" /> on Arbitrum Nova. At 12 seconds per block, that is <Var name="arbOneForceIncludePeriodHours" /> hours and <Var name="novaForceIncludePeriodHours" /> hours.

If the parent chain is itself an Arbitrum chain, as it is for an L3, `block.number` returns the parent chain's estimate of the Ethereum block number. The parent chain's sequencer sets that value, and it stays close to the real Ethereum block number. The window is counted in these Ethereum block numbers. See [Block numbers and time](/arbitrum-essentials/arbitrum-vs-ethereum/block-numbers-and-time#ethereum-or-parent-chain-block-numbers-within-arbitrum).

The parent chain's `block.number` advances only when the parent chain produces blocks. If the parent chain's own sequencer is also down, the L3's window stops advancing until the parent chain produces blocks again.

</Callout>

### When a force inclusion reorders the chain

A force inclusion can cause a <Term id="reorg">reorg</Term> on the child chain. This happens when the sequencer produced blocks it never posted to the parent chain. Those blocks were <Term id="soft-confirmation">soft-confirmed</Term> through the sequencer feed, but the force-included messages now come before them in the Sequencer Inbox.

Every node that follows the sequencer feed reorgs as soon as it reads the empty batch that `forceInclusion` posts to the Sequencer Inbox. It drops the unposted blocks. Soft-confirmed transactions in those blocks can be lost for good:

- **Re-sequencing has a depth limit.** The sequencer re-sequences up to 1,024 dropped messages by default (`node.transaction-streamer.max-reorg-resequence-depth`). It removes any messages beyond that limit.
